title: Optimized Protocol for Coupling Oxygen Consumption Rates with β-Oxidation in Mouse Mitochondria
author: Sánchez-González, Formentini
materials: soleus wash with cold and sterile PBS.
Immediately transfer soleus to cold PBS.

steps.title: Prepare extraction and respiration buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare sufficient volumes of extraction buffer (A) and respiration buffer (B) according to the recipes provided; store both at –20 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Thaw buffers to correct temperatures
steps.instruction: Thaw buffer A on ice (use at 4 °C) and thaw buffer B at 30 °C (use at 30 °C) before any use.

steps.title: Prepare digestion buffer with Nagarse
steps.instruction: Make digestion buffer (C) by adding Nagarse to a final concentration of 0.2 mg mL⁻¹ in buffer A; store at –80 °C for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Pre‑cool equipment and sterilize
steps.instruction: Pre‑cool 1× PBS, beakers, tubes and all surgical material; work inside a laminar‑flow cabinet if possible and spray all surgical items with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Check equipment and remove detergents
steps.instruction: Verify that all equipment functions, pre‑chill centrifuges to 4 °C and ensure no detergent residues are present on potters or glassware.

steps.title: Create sterile working space
steps.instruction: Spray the surgical work area with 70 % ethanol to maintain sterility.

steps.title: Prepare substrate stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make 50× substrate stocks at the concentrations and with the preparations listed below; adjust all stocks to pH 7.4.

substeps.instruction: 1 M malate: dissolve 134 mg in 1 mL milli‑Q H₂O.
1 M glutamate: dissolve 187 mg in 1 mL milli‑Q H₂O; mix 1:1 (v/v) with 1 M malate to obtain a 500 mM glutamate/malate stock.
500 mM succinate: dissolve 59.05 mg in 1 mL milli‑Q H₂O.
50 mM malate: dilute the 1 M malate stock 1:20 with milli‑Q H₂O.
5 mM palmitoyl‑carnitine: dissolve 2.18 mg in 1 mL milli‑Q H₂O.
100 mM ADP: dissolve 42.72 mg in 1 mL milli‑Q H₂O; dilute 1:4 to obtain a 25 mM ADP stock.

Note final substrate concentrations for assays: 10 mM succinate; 10 mM malate + palmitoyl‑carnitine (final 0.5 mM malate, 0.05 mM palmitoyl‑carnitine); 2 mM TMPD + 10 mM ascorbate; 1 M glutamate‑malate (1:1) as NADH‑linked substrate; optional octanoyl‑carnitine or other FFA‑carnitines.

steps.title: Prepare inhibitor stock solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare 100× inhibitor stocks at the concentrations and with the preparations listed; adjust pH to 7.4, store on ice, protect from light and use fresh on the day of the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Rotenone 100 µM stock: dissolve 3.94 mg in 1 mL EtOH to make a 10 mM stock; aliquot, store at –20 °C, dilute 1:100 with milli‑Q H₂O before use (final 1 µM).
Antimycin A 100 µM stock: dissolve 5.34 mg in 1 mL EtOH to make a 10 mM stock; aliquot, store at –20 °C, dilute 1:100 (final 1 µM).
Oligomycin 500 µM stock: dissolve 19.8 mg in 1 mL EtOH to make a 25 mM stock; aliquot, store at –20 °C, dilute 1:50 (final 5 µM).
FCCP 500 µM stock: dissolve 6.35 mg in 1 mL EtOH to make a 25 mM stock; aliquot, store at –20 °C, dilute 1:500 (final 0.5 µM; titrate in 0.25–0.5 µM steps).
Malonate 100 µM final: prepare as needed (final 100 µM).
Sodium azide 100 mM final: prepare as needed (final 100 mM).
KCN 10 µM final (optional): prepare as needed.
Note: EtOH stocks are stable at –20 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Set electrode bath temperature
steps.instruction: Adjust the electrode‑bath temperature to 30 °C; at this temperature the dissolved O₂ concentration is 445 nmol mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Assemble Clark‑type electrode
steps.instruction: Place one drop of saturated KCl on the platinum electrode, immediately cover with a wet Teflon membrane (keep membrane wet throughout), then add milli‑Q water to the working chamber.

steps.title: Power on and start agitation
steps.instruction: Turn on the electrode power, start the computer, launch the Oxygraph+ software, and switch on the stirrer (set to 70 rpm) to ensure homogeneous O₂ concentration.

steps.title: Calibrate electrode with dithionite
steps.instruction: Perform a liquid‑phase calibration at 30 °C and 70 rpm, start recording, add a pinch of dithionite until the trace reaches a plateau (0 % O₂), then save the calibration.

steps.title: Wash electrode chamber
steps.instruction: Rinse the working chamber twice in the following sequence: 2 mL milli‑Q water, 2 mL EtOH, 2 mL milli‑Q water; repeat to remove all dithionite residues.

steps.title: Sacrifice mice
steps.instruction: Euthanize mice in a CO₂ chamber according to approved animal protocols.

steps.title: Extract soleus muscles
steps.instruction: Inside a laminar‑flow cabinet, use pre‑cooled sterile surgical tools to fix the hind‑limb in a flexed position, cover with cold 1× PBS, remove hair, skin and fascia, cut the Achilles tendon, and carefully separate the soleus muscle without any white adipose tissue; note that soleus appears darker red than surrounding muscle.

steps.title: Weigh isolated solei
steps.instruction: Weigh each soleus; typically pool four solei (≈2 mice) to obtain sufficient mitochondria for respiration measurements.

steps.title: Wash soleus in cold PBS
steps.instruction: Place the soleus in a pre‑cooled 50 mL glass beaker and wash with cold 1× PBS.

steps.title: Mince and digest muscle
steps.instruction: Mince the muscle in four volumes (relative to tissue weight) of buffer A (or buffer C if using Nagarse) until the pieces are homogeneous; incubate on ice for 5–10 min to allow Nagarse activity, avoiding longer times that could damage mitochondria.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize the minced tissue in a glass‑glass homogenizer:

substeps.instruction: Do not exceed these numbers to prevent uncoupling.

steps.title: First low‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Transfer the homogenate to pre‑cooled centrifuge tubes and centrifuge 10 min at 700 g, 4 °C; discard the pellet (nuclei and intact cells).

steps.title: Repeat low‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Repeat the 10 min, 700 g, 4 °C centrifugation once more to improve mitochondrial purity; discard the second pellet.

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation for mitochondria
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the combined supernatants 10 min at 10,000 g, 4 °C; discard the supernatant and keep the mitochondrial pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend mitochondrial pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the mitochondria‑enriched pellet in 100 µL of respiration buffer (B) and keep on ice at all times.

steps.title: Determine protein concentration
steps.instruction: Measure mitochondrial protein concentration using the Bradford assay on a spectrophotometer; use buffer B for the calibration curve because it may interfere with the assay, and keep all samples on ice.
